extracted.intended_audience: press officers, communications professionals, science writers, and editors who prepare science news releases for journals, research institutions, and funders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing accurate, accessible science news releases that alert reporters and the public to research findings, including preparation, structure, review, and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Your goal — Are you targeting a journal's core readers, funding agencies, or peer institutions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before writing, decide what you want the release to accomplish (e.g., reach reporters, inform funders, raise institutional profile) so the tone, emphasis, and distribution can be tailored appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Your audience — Who needs to understand this research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the primary audiences (specialist reporters, general public, disciplinary peers, funders) to determine level of technical detail, vocabulary, and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the journal article thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the journal article thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base the release on a careful reading of the paper to ensure accurate representation of aims, methods, findings, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview the research team
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview the research team about their central question, key findings, surprises, and real-world context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask researchers about the central question, the key results, unexpected findings, and the practical or conceptual context to extract quotable, clarifying material and avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situate the work in existing knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand how the work fits into existing knowledge and what questions remain
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain significance by relating the study to prior work and by noting unresolved questions or limitations so readers and reporters can assess novelty and importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: concise, catchy, and intellectually honest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Headline must be "concise, catchy, and intellectually honest." Avoid hype while capturing reader interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a short, engaging headline that accurately reflects findings; do not overstate implications or introduce sensational claims. Balance attention-grabbing phrasing with fidelity to the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: state what's interesting and why now
rubrics_metrics.description: The lede must tell readers what's interesting about the story and why you're telling them about it now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a clear, accessible sentence that highlights the main takeaway and timeliness. Avoid technical jargon in the opening; use accessible language while maintaining accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Research question being addressed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early in the body, state the question or problem the researchers investigated so readers understand the study's purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize findings concisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Concise description of findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the key results succinctly and clearly, emphasizing the main conclusions without overgeneralizing beyond what the data support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain importance and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Importance and context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe why the findings matter, who they affect, and how they relate to broader issues or prior research to give readers a sense of relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Methodology used
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly explain how the study was conducted (design, sample, key methods) at a level appropriate for the intended audience so reporters can evaluate credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: State study limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Study limitations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly acknowledge limitations (scope, sample size, generalizability, potential confounds) to avoid misleading readers and to prevent exaggeration in downstream coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note future research directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Future research directions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate next steps or open questions that follow from the study to provide context about the study's place in an ongoing research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide researcher names and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Researcher names and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List lead and corresponding authors and their institutional affiliations so reporters can attribute work and contact experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include publication details and journal link
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Publication details with journal link
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give full citation information and a direct link to the journal article to facilitate verification and follow-up reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: Funding sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List grant numbers and funding organizations to make potential conflicts of interest and support transparent for readers and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include at least one researcher quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Body Content: At least one researcher quote
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide one or more short, clear quotes from authors that humanize the research and offer authoritative interpretation; ensure quotes are checked with the researcher for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length: be concise but complete
rubrics_metrics.description: "A news release should be as long as it needs to be—say what you need to say and then stop."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep releases as short as possible while including necessary information; avoid padding or unnecessary technical digressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define technical terms and use consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Define technical terms when first introducing them, then use terminology consistently throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce and briefly explain specialized terms at first use so nonexperts can follow, and thereafter use the same terms to avoid reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher review for technical accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Researcher review — Authors must verify technical accuracy and context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have authors/researchers review the release to confirm factual accuracy and appropriate emphasis; this step prevents errors but should not permit unchecked expansion of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial editing for clarity and error-catching
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial editing — Third-party editing ensures clarity and catches errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject the release to editorial review to improve readability, correct language issues, and ensure that the release communicates effectively to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance accessibility with researcher input
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance — Maintain accessibility while incorporating researcher feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve tensions between simplifying for readers and preserving technical nuance by negotiating with researchers and using explicit caveats where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid hype and exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid hype — Exaggerations in news releases are reflected in subsequent news stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about causal language and broad claims; make limitations and uncertainty explicit to reduce the chance of sensationalized media coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution via multiple channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution Strategy — Publish on organizational newsroom websites; send to reporter mailing lists; contact reporters individually; share with funding agencies; post to distribution sites; feed content to news aggregators
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mix of owned channels (newsroom site), targeted outreach (beat reporters), curated services (EurekAlert, AlphaGalileo, Newswise), funder networks, and aggregators to maximize reach and appropriate amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core ethical principle: honesty and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Yes, a news release must be honest and accurate about the research—that is nonnegotiable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat factual accuracy and intellectual honesty as mandatory constraints on writing and editing; do not compromise accuracy for attention or publicity.
